steps.title: Age with be, phone numbers and emails

explanation.en: In English, age uses the verb be, not have: 'I'm 25' or 'I'm 25 years old' — never 'I have 25 years'. Ask: 'How old are you?'. Phone numbers are said digit by digit, in groups, and 0 is usually 'oh'. In email addresses @ is 'at' and . is 'dot'. Numbers from 21 to 99 have a hyphen in writing: twenty-one, forty-five.
explanation.es: En inglés la edad usa el verbo be, no have: «I'm 25» o «I'm 25 years old»; nunca «I have 25 years». Se pregunta «How old are you?». Los teléfonos se dicen dígito a dígito, por grupos, y el 0 suele ser «oh». En los correos @ es «at» y . es «dot». Del 21 al 99 se escriben con guion: twenty-one, forty-five.

examples.en: My phone number is three one oh, five five two, eight four seven one.
My email is ana dot ruiz at mail dot com.

watchOut.en: 'I have 30 years' ✗ → 'I'm 30' ✓. And 'forty' has no 'u' (four → forty).
watchOut.es: «I have 30 years» ✗ → «I'm 30» ✓. Y «forty» no lleva «u» (four → forty).

steps.title: /θ/ in three and -teen vs -ty
steps.focus: /θ/ (three, thirty) and stress: thir-TEEN vs THIR-ty

tip.en: /θ/: tongue tip between your teeth, blow air, no voice — not /t/ ('tree') and not /s/. -teen numbers have stress at the end and a long /iː/: thir-TEEN. -ty numbers have stress at the start: THIR-ty, with a short ending. Make -teen endings long and clear so people don't hear 30.
tip.es: /θ/: punta de la lengua entre los dientes, sopla aire sin voz; no /t/ («tree») ni /s/. Los -teen llevan el acento al final con /iː/ larga: thir-TEEN. Los -ty al inicio: THIR-ty, con final corto. Alarga bien los -teen para que no se entienda 30.
